intro: Cartographer Renna unrolls a chart that is mostly grey. 'The bay behind the Shelf, under fog. Four things lie out there, and our chart says nothing about any of them. Each square you sound costs a boat trip, and we have sixteen trips before the tide turns.'
reportsIntro: Harbourkeeper Sora drops three shells on the chart. 'Sailors' reports. People tell me things on the quay. I am not saying they are all true.'

claims.name: a reef
claims.claim: A reef runs along the north edge of the bay.
claims.support: Two soundings at two fathoms, and white water seen over it at low tide. Measured, by us, today.

claims.name: a deep channel
claims.claim: A safe channel runs down the east side.
claims.support: The ferry crew has taken this way every week for ten years. Nobody measured it. They know it with their hands on the oars.

claims.name: an old wreck
claims.claim: A wreck lies off the west point.
claims.support: One diver's report, from one dive, written down the same day. Nobody has dived there since.

claims.name: a sandbar
claims.claim: A sandbar lies across the south mouth, and it moves.
claims.support: Charts from three summers show it in three places. No one chart is wrong. Together they show that it moves.

reports.text: A fisher: 'Our nets tore on something sharp near the north edge.'
The ferry cook: 'We always go down the east side. Always.'
A visiting captain: 'There is a rock in the middle of that bay. I am sure of it.'

falseReport: Open water where the captain's rock should be. Sora winces. 'He was sure. Being sure is not a sounding.'
trueReport: The lead line confirms what the sailor said. Sora marks the shell: 'Reported, then sounded. Both.'

kinds.measurement: Renna: 'Our own lead line. I trust this most, for today. A reef does not move much.'
kinds.practice: Sora: 'Ten years of crossings is a kind of sounding too, done slowly, by people whose lives depended on it.'
kinds.testimony: Renna: 'One person, once. Honest, I think. But I would print it with the diver's name and the date.'
kinds.records: Sora: 'Three old charts that disagree, and they are all right. The disagreement is the finding.'

endFull: The fog lifts a little. All four are on the chart, each with what holds it up.
endShort: The tide turns and the boats come in. Some of the bay is still grey. That is the chart you have.

prints.text: Print only what we sounded ourselves
prints.reply: Renna nods. 'Clean and honest. But the ferry crew will laugh at a chart that leaves out the channel they use every week.'

prints.text: Print the rest as dotted lines, with who said it and when
prints.reply: Sora smiles. 'A dotted line is a promise to check. Sailors can read that. It says how we know, not only what we know.'

prints.text: Print it all solid: sailors need a full chart
prints.reply: Renna is quiet a moment. 'A full chart is what people ask for. If the captain's rock goes on it solid, every boat will steer round open water, and nobody will ever check.'
